title: A learned twelve-gene signature stratifies lung-adenocarcinoma survival in archived cohorts
summary: Cox screening and random-survival-forest selection identified a twelve-gene immune-related score associated with overall survival in 954 lung-adenocarcinoma patients across four archived datasets. A 204-patient discovery cohort was followed by GEO validation cohorts totaling 309 patients and a 441-patient TCGA cohort; high-score groups had worse survival and distinct inferred immune profiles. Validation used a separate median cutoff in each cohort, and these retrospective associations do not demonstrate treatment-response prediction, clinical benefit or causal immune mechanisms.
ai_technology: Random survival forest variable hunting; Cox regression risk scoring

evidence.tested: GSE31210 supplied 204 discovery patients; GSE41271 and GSE50081 supplied 309 validation patients, and TCGA supplied 441. Cox screening followed by random-survival-forest selection produced twelve genes for a Cox-weighted score. High-score groups had worse survival in both validation groups (reported HR 1.66 in GEO and 1.93 in TCGA); inferred immune profiles were also compared.
evidence.unknown: Each validation cohort used its own median cutoff, so this is not locked-threshold clinical validation. The authors identify the retrospective design and absence of immunotherapy-response data as limitations and call for prospective validation. Immune abundance is inferred and associations do not establish causality. An inconsistent GEO AUC/confidence-interval sentence is not used for performance claims.
evidence.ai_role: A random survival forest selects prognostic immune-related genes after Cox screening; the selected genes define the survival-risk score whose associations and immune profiles are tested in archived clinical datasets.

source_review.scope: Original full-text source: abstract, publication metadata, relevant model/feature selection and validation Methods, Results and limitations. Supplementary files not assessed.
